name: Double Klondike
description: Double Klondike is a challenging two-deck variation of the world-famous Klondike Solitaire. By using 104 cards, the game features a larger tableau of nine columns and eight foundation piles. While the fundamental rules of alternating colors and building sequences remain the same, the increased volume of cards creates more opportunities for advanced maneuvering and sequencing.

history.origins: Klondike itself originated during the 19th-century gold rush in the Yukon. The 'Double' version emerged in the early 20th century as players sought a more complex and longer-lasting challenge than the standard 52-card version.
timeline: Late 1800s: Standard Klondike becomes popular in mining camps.
1920s: Double-deck solitaire variations begin appearing in rulebooks like Hoyle.
1990s: Becomes a staple in digital solitaire collections on personal computers.
history.cultural: Often played as a relaxing yet mentally stimulating solo activity; recognized as one of the most popular 'big' solitaire games.
history.evolution: The expansion from 7 to 9 tableau columns was designed to maintain the balance of hidden cards while providing enough 'legal move' space for the 104-card deck.

setup.players: One player (solitaire). The player works alone with two combined 52-card decks, building the tableau of nine columns and eight foundation piles until all 104 cards are moved to the foundations.
setup.dealing: Deal 9 tableau columns: Column 1 has 1 card, Column 2 has 2, ..., Column 9 has 9 cards. Only the top card of each column is face-up. Remaining cards form the Stock.
setup.equipment: Two card decks, large playing surface.

rules.objective: Move all 104 cards to the 8 foundation piles (2 for each suit), building each suit from Ace to King.
rules.gameplay:
1. Building the Tableau: You can move cards within the tableau to build sequences in alternating colors (e.g., a Black 7 on a Red 8).
2. Foundations: Move Aces to the foundations as soon as they become available. Build foundations UP by suit (A-2-3...K).
3. The Stock: Flip cards from the stock (usually 3 at a time) to find moves. In some variations, you can only go through the stock once.
keyRules: Only a King (or a sequence starting with a King) can be moved into an empty tableau space.
Whole sequences can be moved as long as the bottom card follows the alternating-color rule for the target column.
There are 8 foundation slots; each suit must be completed twice.

strategy.basic: Always prioritize uncovering hidden cards in the tableau over drawing from the stock.
strategy.intermediate: Empty slots: Do not create an empty column unless you have a King ready to fill it, as empty columns are the only way to move large card blocks.
strategy.advanced: Foundation Balance: Build the foundation piles evenly. If you move one Red suit to the foundations but leave the other Red suit in the tableau, you may block your ability to move Black cards in the tableau.
tips: Keep the foundations balanced between the two copies of each suit.
Scan all 9 columns before every stock draw; it's easy to miss a lead with so many cards in play.
